text:
Maria: Quick async standup — Orbit slice at 3% running against model_v2. Health checks are green but p95 latency is up ~40ms over the last hour. Blocker: decision needed on whether to ramp the gamma feature flag to 10% or hold. Last deploy was at 08:12 by deploy-bot.

Josh: Can you paste the exact p95 and error rate deltas? Is this looking like a model perf regression or infra noise?

Maria: Metrics snapshot:```
p95_before=210ms -> p95_now=250ms
error_rate_before=0.12% -> error_rate_now=0.14%
requests_per_min=1.2k
```Small but noticeable. No user-facing 5xx spike yet.

Sophia: I noticed increased KV cache evictions around 08:05 — sending logs: https://logs.company/infra/evictions?range=30m :mag_right:

Kevin: If we have evictions, could be working set growth from longer sequences. Suggest either temporarily drop batch_size 64->32 for the orbit slice or pause the gamma ramp. I'm +hold on ->10% until we confirm.

Anya: Checked the node metrics — one runtime pod had a CPU spike to 82% coinciding with the latency bump. I'm cordoning that pod and restarting the runtime process now, will monitor.

deploy-bot: Canary event: orbit-slice (model_v2) remains at 3% (no new deploys). Rollout window: 07:00-12:00 UTC.

Maria: OK I'll hold the gamma ramp at 3% for now. Thanks @Anya for taking action. Plan: wait 15m post-restart, re-evaluate p95 and error rate, then decide on 5% try tomorrow morning. :thumbsup:

Josh: Also quick ping — CR #342 (infra: adaptive-batching) needs review. Low-risk changes, tagging @Sophia @Kevin for a quick look.

Sophia: I'll review CR #342 after I finish the logs check (ETA ~30m).

Kevin: Skimming the diff now — looks fine, one comment about a null-check. Will approve once Maria confirms regression is gone.

Maria: Update: Anya restarted the runtime pod at 08:40, p95 dropped to ~212ms and error rate back to 0.13%. Uncordoned and monitoring. Holding ramp; will re-open tomorrow for 5% if stable. Thanks everyone.

Maria: (final) marking this thread for follow-up in the morning if anything changes.
